attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his own birthday-observations list on his Substack.

semantics.note: Two firm present-tense observations: companies are starting to temper expectations, and many initial expectations were unrealistic. The normalisation keeps both parts and the LLM-adoption context.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. 'Starting' sets no majority threshold, 'many' sets no number, and the window from early 2024 to publication is reasonable. The support condition fairly requires both parts of the claim.

evidence.note: A secondary reproduction of Bain's February 2024 survey, published before the cutoff. It shows a shift from hype to more realistic assessments, which supports the moderation part. It reports only a small shortfall against expectations, so it is weak on 'many unrealistic'.
February 2024 interviews with 15 executives describe setting realistic expectations as a common challenge. They do not measure revisions or compare initial expectations with results.
Fieldwork from October to December 2023 predates the target period. It shows high baseline expectations and does not test whether moderation began by March 2024.

reviews.rationale: e1 credibly supports an emerging shift from hype to more realistic assessment by February 2024. The second part, that many initial expectations were unrealistic, is not established: e1 reports only a small shortfall against expectations, and e2 is qualitative and undated. Nothing contradicts the claim. Because the support condition requires both parts, the packet does not settle the claim.
